clue.text: Alcoholic drink on bar in box with a certain style

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: a counter is the bar in a pub or shop
punch is a mixed alcoholic drink served from a bowl

explanation.surface: Someone orders a boozy drink at the bar, dressed with a certain flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' looks like a container but is the verb to fight with fists.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterpunch is to fight by returning blows, a particular boxing technique.

clue.text: Cold beer's flavouring in the mouth

definitions.note: chops is a plural noun for the jaws or mouth

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
hops give beer its bitter flavour

explanation.surface: A chilled beer leaves its taste lingering on the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Chops is slang for the jaws and mouth, as in licking one's chops.

clue.text: Constantly going on about British firm

indicators.note: here the longer word goes about, or around, the letter for British

parts.note: unending means continuing without stop

explanation.surface: A British company that never stops talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective meaning resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm in the sense of resolute and unyielding, refusing to change one's position.

clue.text: Fix match — agree about bagging wicket

parts.note: a tie is a match or fixture, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: bagging means pocketing, so the turned word holds the wicket letter
about tells us to turn the word for agree round

parts.note: to nod is to show agreement
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: Accusations of match-fixing in cricket: arranging a result around taking a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix match' suggests rigging a game; Fix alone is the definition. NOD turned about gives DON, which bags W to make DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie down is to secure or fasten something firmly in place.

clue.text: One filling roll for party

indicators.note: the numeral fills the list word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone putting the filling into a bread roll for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' suggests bread; it is a list of names.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, to party in a boisterous way.

clue.text: Bit of fungus in American's soup, not good

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for good

parts.note: gumbo is a thick soup or stew from the American South

explanation.surface: A disappointing bowl of mushroom soup in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: Gumbo is a Louisiana stew thickened with okra.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbo is the raised central boss on the cap of a mushroom.

clue.text: Grumbled this person repeatedly rejected proactive advice

parts.note: carped means complained or grumbled

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the two pronouns read backwards

parts.note: this person, said by the speaker, is ME and also I: two ways of saying it

explanation.surface: A grumbler keeps turning down well-meant advice to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' is both ME and I, which is why it appears twice, and 'rejected' sends both backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpe diem, Latin for seize the day, urges acting now rather than waiting.

clue.text: Drama's opening — I'm not sure Antony and Cleopatra lost here

parts.note: a play opens with Act I
um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Uncertainty about how Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama's opening' looks like the first letter D; it is Act I, the opening act.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony and Cleopatra's fleet was defeated by Octavian at the naval battle of Actium in 31 BC.

clue.text: Cut the grass again and again?

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Mowing the lawn once more, and then once more after that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut the grass again' reads as mowing; the definition is 'again and again', which is once plus twice more, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something, then again and again, makes three times in all.

clue.text: Love-filled groom in depression

indicators.note: filled means the grooming word has the zero put inside it

parts.note: to comb hair is to groom it
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A bridegroom full of love, yet sunk in gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' and 'depression' suggest a gloomy bridegroom; depression is a hollow in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a short valley or hollow on a hillside, a geographical depression.

clue.text: Dine out? Hot food from the east is capital

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged
in an across clue, read from the east means from right to left

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Eating out on spicy Asian food in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns DINE into EDIN; H plus GRUB read from the east gives BURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland.

clue.text: Details a lot of foolish questions book ignored

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: insane can mean very foolish

indicators.note: ignored tells us to leave the book letter out

parts.note: doubts are questions or misgivings

explanation.surface: Someone asks many silly questions and pays no attention to the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes the last letter off INSANE to give INSAN; DOUBTS with B ignored gives DOUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ins and outs of something are its finer points and particulars.

clue.text: Short trousers revealing figure back in biblical times

indicators.note: short means the brand name is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: Levis are a well-known brand of denim jeans

explanation.surface: Shorts that expose a number on the back, in biblical times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short trousers' suggests shorts; Short is the signal to drop the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was a son of Jacob, founder of the priestly tribe in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Fail to score at home, gathering round goal

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit the target

indicators.note: gathering means the at-home word collects the round letter inside it

parts.note: in means at home
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A footballer misses at a home game while players crowd round the goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface uses goal as a target to score in; it is the definition, meaning an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is an assigned task or aim, much like an objective.

clue.text: Chaplains interpreted passage with great craft

indicators.note: interpreted means read differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chaplains skilfully interpreting a passage of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great craft' suggests skill; here craft means large vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship canal is a waterway wide and deep enough for ocean-going vessels.

clue.text: Fence in play area English struggle to get knocked over

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a playground or park

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: An English fence round a playground gets toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like a barrier; it is the verb to deal in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive stolen goods is what a fence, a dealer in stolen property, does.

clue.text: Designed schematic Q&A session

indicators.note: designed means arranged or laid out anew, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Planning a question-and-answer session in diagram form.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism teaches religious doctrine through a fixed series of questions and answers.

clue.text: Stones record captures hearts

indicators.note: captures means the record word holds the card letter inside

parts.note: a single is a record with one song
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones' record wins people's hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' and 'record' suggest the rock band; stones means pebbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles on a beach.

clue.text: Stew, small bit of meal left by king

indicators.note: left by means the king letter departs from the meal word

parts.note: a course is one part of a meal
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A king leaves behind a scrap of his stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse is a meat and vegetable stew, the traditional dish of Liverpool.

clue.text: Caught EastEnders' highly cultural feature

indicators.note: caught means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: highbrow means highly cultured; East Enders, as Cockneys, drop their aitches when they say it

explanation.surface: A highbrow moment caught in the TV soap EastEnders.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End, where the Cockney accent drops the H from highbrow.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is one of the facial features, the arch of hair above the eye.

clue.text: Supplier of DC current that's too variable in basic lodgings to the west

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the reversed lodgings
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: a camp provides simple accommodation

indicators.note: variable means changeable, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tangle about electrical direct current running too erratically in a rough camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'DC current' suggests electricity; DC is Washington, and current is a river flow. The jumbled TOO goes inside PMAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac river flows past Washington DC, bringing its water current.

clue.text: A pair of Zulus in China love swanky residence

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
Zulu is the radio alphabet word for Z, so two of them
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Two Zulus in China enjoying a grand home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is rhyming slang for a mate. The pieces simply run in sequence after PAL, so 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A palazzo is an Italian palace or grand mansion.

clue.text: Record-breaking queen in a state of inebriation

indicators.note: breaking means the queen splits the record in two

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record
Anne was Queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A queen sets a record while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-breaking' reads as a feat; here the queen breaks into the disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned is slang for drunk.

clue.text: Seat leading Conservative lost generating anguished remark

indicators.note: lost tells us that letter is removed from the seat

parts.note: a couch is a seat

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative who loses a parliamentary seat cries out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' and 'Conservative' suggest an election; a seat is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is an exclamation of sudden pain.

clue.text: Official choosing to ignore first instance of base work of The Mirror?

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a sports official

indicators.note: to ignore means to leave these letters out

parts.note: selection is the act of choosing
first stands for the opening letter of the choosing word
e is a mathematical base, that of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A referee rejects the tabloid's lowbrow output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Mirror' is a British tabloid newspaper; here it is just a looking glass. SELECTION loses its first letter and an E.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror's job is to show back an image, so a reflection is what it produces.

clue.text: Two places to save one due to get sacrificed

parts.note: the clue's two places to save money; the first is an ISA, an individual savings account, a British tax-free scheme
completes the two places to save; the second is an A/C, the usual short form of account

explanation.surface: Two places, rescuing one person due to be sacrificed.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account; AC is short for account.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abraham was told to offer his son as a sacrifice before an angel intervened.

clue.text: Save energy — it's basic

parts.note: save and bar both mean except
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An eco-slogan: saving energy is fundamental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save energy' reads as conservation; save here means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means plain and minimal, just the essentials.

clue.text: Seasonal deliveryman reported pleasure trip in resort

parts.note: Santa delivers presents at Christmas

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a cruise is a holiday voyage

explanation.surface: Father Christmas reportedly took a cruise to a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Cruz is a seaside town in California, also in Tenerife, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Silly way programme and performance end

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically and split 2,2,1: the way each of these two words finishes, with the same vowel

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'way programme and performance end' as a description: both words end in an E, which split 2,2,1 spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means foolish and senseless, lacking any sense or substance.

clue.text: Group has e.g. driver installed in fast computer

indicators.note: installed in means the golf club is placed inside

parts.note: fleet means swift or fast
a Mac is an Apple computer
a driver is an example of a wood in golf

explanation.surface: A band has a chauffeur fitted into a speedy computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist; it is a golf club, one of the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleetwood Mac is the rock band behind the album Rumours.
